hooks.name: Record optimisation reasoning
hooks.description: Prompts for an OPTIMISATION-LOG.md entry whenever timing, caching, pre-warming, or concurrency code is touched, so the reasoning behind each performance decision is captured rather than only its outcome.

action.prompt:
You just modified timing, browser-pool, pre-warming, or session-orchestration code — the areas where performance changes live.

If this change was made for performance reasons, append an entry to docs/OPTIMISATION-LOG.md before you finish. Use the O-NN template at the top of that file, and make sure it answers:

- What was the measured problem? Include the before number.
- What options did you consider, including the ones you did not take?
- WHY did you choose this one first? Cost to try, cost to undo, evidence available. This is the most valuable field — the order of attempts is what future readers need.
- What was the measured result? After number.
- If it failed or was superseded: why, and what did the failure reveal?

Rules:
- Every performance claim needs a measured number from data/metrics.jsonl or a reproduced experiment. If you cannot measure it, say so rather than estimating — one unmeasured estimate in this file was wrong by 3x and mis-sized the next decision.
- Record failed approaches. Do not quietly replace a failed attempt with a working one; the failure is usually what revealed the right answer.
- If you rejected an approach, add it to the "Rejected approaches" table with the reason, so nobody re-runs the experiment.
- If the change also fixed a defect, add a separate F-NN entry to docs/ENGINEERING-LOG.md and cross-reference.

Skip this only if the change was a pure refactor with no performance intent and no behavioural lesson.
